children: Our Bureau Mumbai: Global investment firm Brookfield will invest up to $600 million (5,743 crore) in ACME Cleantech Ventures, the green molecules platform of ACME Group, to fund the development and construction of projects in India and the Gulf.

The investment marks Brookfield's entry into the green molecules sector in the region. It will be made through Brookfield Global Transition Fund, which focuses on investments supporting the transition to a net-zero carbon economy. ACME Cleantech Ventures, a UK-based entity within the ACME Group, is dedicated to the group's green molecules business.

The platform is developing a pipeline of green ammonia and green methanol projects in India and Oman. "The demand for green molecules continues to grow as companies and governments seek scalable solutions to decarbonize while strengthening energy security," said Nawal Saini, managing partner and head of energy, South Asia and the Middle East, Brookfield.

ACME said the investment would support the expansion of its green molecules platform and help develop projects aimed at supplying clean fuels and feedstock to domestic and international markets. The company has secured offtake partnerships with global and Indian companies, including Yara International, IHI Corporation, Mitsubishi Gas Chemicals, Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI), IFFCO, Paradeep Phosphates, Coromandel International and Indorama India.

ACME currently has an operational green ammonia facility in Bikaner, Rajasthan, and is developing a green ammonia project in Duqm, Oman. It is also establishing new facilities in Odisha following its green ammonia purchase agreement with SECI, alongside a joint venture with Japan's IHI Corporation and an offtake agreement with Mitsubishi Gas Chemicals.

title: Brookfield to Invest Up to $600M in ACME's Green Molecules Biz
